# lazy-layers-cache

> A TypeScript layered cache for Node.js and Cloudflare Workers, with Redis or Cloudflare KV as L2.

## What is lazy-layers-cache?

lazy-layers-cache is a Promise-based caching library with in-memory L1 and an optional Redis or Cloudflare KV L2. Node.js uses the main entrypoint. Cloudflare Workers use the small `lazy-layers-cache/cloudflare` entrypoint.

For Cloudflare KV, `getOrSet` loads on a miss, with in-flight deduplication inside one Worker cache or Node.js process. KV has no cross-instance loader lease. A dedicated application Queue retries KV deletions after `invalidate` or `invalidateByPattern`; it does not fan out to every Worker's L1. Cloudflare Event Subscriptions cover platform lifecycle events, not cache keys. See https://lazy-layers-cache.vercel.app/docs/setups/cloudflare-kv.

Two methods do almost all the work:
- `getOrSet(key, loader)` — read through the layers and call the loader on a miss. Node.js Redis buses can prime peers; Cloudflare KV does not.
- `delete(key)` / `invalidate(key)` — delete the key. Peer L1 behavior depends on the configured bus and runtime.

## Key Features

- Lazy loading with getOrSet and local in-flight deduplication
- Cloudflare KV L2 from Workers bindings or the Node.js REST adapter
- Scoped `invalidateByPattern` and a dedicated Cloudflare Queue retry consumer
- In-flight promise deduplication prevents same-process stampede
- Automatic Redis-backed locking and renewal for cold and expired keys across instances
- Fail-open resilience: L2 and event-bus failures are logged and swallowed, local L1 continues serving
- Stale fallback: last-known-good values returned on loader errors or timeouts
- Negative caching: loader misses briefly cached to avoid hammering databases
- Circuit breakers for L2 and event-bus publish
- Soft and hard timeouts
- Distributed invalidation over Redis Pub/Sub, RabbitMQ, NATS Core, or NATS JetStream
- Size-tiered compression: none (< 256 B), lz4 (256 B–4 KB), zstd (4 KB+)
- 20+ typed cache events for metrics, logs, and tracing
- Live observability dashboard with Prometheus + OpenTelemetry
- TypeScript native, ESM and CommonJS

## Quick Start

```bash
npm install lazy-layers-cache
```

```ts
import { LazyLayersCache } from "lazy-layers-cache";

const cache = new LazyLayersCache<string, User>({
  ttlMs: 60_000,
  levels: { L1: { maxEntries: 1_000, ttlMs: 10_000 } },
  inflight: { enabled: true, ttlMs: 5_000 },
});

const user = await cache.getOrSet(`user:${id}`, async () => {
  return db.users.findById(id);
});
```

## Serialization Tiers

| Size | Codec | Wire prefix | Why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| < 256 B | none | HC1M | Compression makes small payloads bigger |
| 256 B – 4 KB | lz4 | HC1L | Smaller and ~5x faster than zstd at these sizes |
| 4 KB+ | zstd | HC1Z | Best ratio at scale; falls back to lz4 on Node 20 |
